newsitem.title: USA: Christopher voices deep concern at W. Bank clashes.
newsitem.headline: Christopher voices deep concern at W. Bank clashes.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Wednesday expressed "deep concern" over bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians and called on the two sides to return to the negotiating table.

Christopher said he had telephoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Paris to urge him to try to calm the situation and that U.S. officials had also contacted Palestinian President Yasser Arafat with the same message.

A senior PLO official said Israeli troops had killed seven Palestinians in Ramallah during the bloodiest clashes in the West Bank since PLO rule began. The violence erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near a sacred Islamic site in Jerusalem.
"We've been following the situation last night and today with deep concern," Christopher said, answering questions before a meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.

"We have urged the parties to defuse the situation, to restore calm in the area -- that's what needs to be done now. They should return to the negotiating table and make progress on the significant issues before them," he added.

Christopher said he had spoken to Netanyahu about two hours previously "and urged him, as we've been urging chairman Arafat, to take steps to calm the situation". U.S. officials said U.S. special Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross had spoken to Arafat.
